title: Volume 1 - Chapter 7: The Opponent
content: Chapter 7: The Opponent
“Negative thinking distances a person from achieving their goals... What’s important is the image of success and a positive attitude.”

During breaks in training, it had become my routine to read the book Louise recommended. Apparently, what I lacked was positive thinking. Having been taught to always assume the worst and act cautiously, this was a surprising concept to me. I couldn’t fully believe that simply imagining myself improving my magic power output would lead to success.
As I turned the page, I found an answer to my feelings.
“What matters is the heart that believes. You must not doubt... Hmph, do I really lack everything?”

I let my guard down since no one was around and slipped into using “ore” (a masculine first-person pronoun). I usually tried to be careful about that, but I guess I was really cornered. Just as I was concentrating on reading, I noticed footsteps and looked up.
Dr. Allison was walking toward me.
“Ren Hifumi, about the third magic converter output experiment... What’s that book you’re reading?”
She cast a suspicious glance at the title of the book I was holding.
“A friend in my class recommended it. Apparently, I lack positive thinking, and they advised me that might be causing my magic power output to drop.”
Dr. Allison looked doubtful, but when the topic turned to magic power, her expression grew serious.
“Your mindset... in this case, your mental strength, right? I was considering an approach from the psychological side, but if a Valkyrie says it, that’s convincing.”
“Yes.”
I closed the book, marking the page, and Dr. Allison looked at the cover.
“I thought you’d turned to self-help books because of repeated failures. I was worried.”
I stood up from the bench and straightened my posture.
“This is my first time reading this kind of book, but it’s been educational.”
“I see. But what surprised me more was that you made a friend. I was worried you’d be isolated in class and stressed.”
“Warrant Officer Louise is cooperative and kind.”
“Friendships are important. Depending on the situation, I might allow you to share some information about the experiments. That way, you can extract more accurate information.”
“Is that really okay?”

“If it leads to results, I’ll overlook it this time. But only with that friend. — Back to the matter at hand, the date for the third experiment has been set. The target this time is one percent output.”
The initial goal had been ten percent, but by the third experiment, it had dropped to one percent. This simply meant their expectations of me had fallen.
“I’ll do my best to meet the target by the scheduled date!”
“That would be helpful.”
Dr. Allison turned her back and walked away. I sat back down on the bench and opened the book to continue reading.
“Next is... how to imagine your successful self.”
I pictured the Thunderbolt outputting the specified magic power and generating its force field.
“Imagine your successful self... imagine...”
I trained relentlessly to perfect that image by the scheduled date.
“This is the start of the third magic power output experiment. Pilot, are you ready?”
Starting the third magic converter experiment, I gripped the control stick tightly.
“Yes, no problems.”

This time, I had read the book Louise recommended and devoured related books of the same kind. I had imagined my successful self over and over. To improve my negative personality, I tried every training method written in the book. Now, all that remained was for me to deliver results.
Dr. Allison appeared on the monitor, looking somewhat exasperated.
“You’re more motivated than usual. Can I assume the books helped?”
“I’ve done everything I could.”
I had been taught at the training facility that preparation was key. Until the experiment day, I had read self-help books thoroughly and put their advice into practice.
“You seem confident. I hope it leads to results. Starting the experiment now. Pilot, begin magic power supply.”
“Starting magic power supply!”
I clenched the control stick and released magic power... Magic flowed into the converter, and the output needle twitched.
I felt intuitively that more magic power was being released than last time.
I can do this... This time, I will succeed!
I banished the image of failure and pictured only success.
“...Experiment complete.”
When the experiment ended, I immediately asked Dr. Allison for the results.
“What are the results? Dr. Allison, how did it go?”
My voice grew louder from impatience. I wanted to know the results as soon as possible. That much, I felt confident about this experiment.
But from Dr. Allison’s expression, it was clear the results were not good.
“Looking at the numbers alone, the effect was nearly three times greater.”
“Three times?”
Although the numbers showed a significant increase, it wasn’t the result I wanted.
“Yes, three times. But to be clear, it didn’t reach one percent. Three times is great, but it’s still within the margin of error.”
“Within the... margin of error...”
Despite reading self-help books and trying a psychological approach, the results were disappointing.
Dr. Allison announced the continuation of the experiments.
“If it keeps increasing, there’s potential. We’ll start the second experiment of the day now.”
“...Understood.”
Right, I just have to keep producing results. As long as I keep showing progress...
Reviewing the third experiment’s results, Dr. Allison and Dr. Smith exchanged opinions.
Dr. Smith commented on the results.
“At first, the output was three times the last experiment, but it got worse with each attempt. Maybe you exhausted your magic power on the first try?”
He accepted the results without anger or regret. To Allison, his carefree attitude was infuriating.
“There’s hope in the slight increase, but the upper management will just see it as error.”
If the upper management judged the Prometheus Project a failure, our development team would be disbanded. Allison wanted him to feel the urgency, but Dr. Smith just laughed.
“The results are improving, aren’t they? If we keep the psychological approach, maybe we can reach the one percent target.”
“The original goal was ten percent! If reading self-help books was enough for success, it wouldn’t be such a struggle.”
He didn’t deny Ren’s efforts considering the psychological approach’s potential. But the results were still within the margin of error.
From Allison’s perspective, self-help books lacked scientific basis. She wanted to stop it if she could.
“Imagining success solves everything? That’s occult nonsense.”
Dr. Smith listened to Allison but expressed his own view.

“Imagining success alone isn’t enough. Scientifically, the process leading to success is also important. Above all, execution is key. It’s premature to call it occult. It’s just lacking explanation. From now on, we should tell Envy to focus on the process. What matters is the right effort that leads to results.”
His ambiguous words were neither wrong nor right. Allison retorted with sarcasm.
“The process is important for success... Exactly. If there were no problems with that process, I’d wholeheartedly agree.”
We want to improve magic power output, but without knowing how, it’s hard to act. Ren and the development team were still groping for the method.
Ignoring Allison’s sour mood, Dr. Smith stared at the numbers from the latest results.
“Now then, how do we achieve the target from here?”
“Ehhh! It failed!?”
To report the failed experiment, I had come to the rooftop with Louise. She voiced her surprise at the results, and I felt sorry.
“Even though I got advice from you, Louise, it ended in a disappointing result. It’s all my fault. I couldn’t strongly imagine my successful self.”
Unconsciously, I doubted myself. At first, I felt a glimmer of hope, but the results showed I was far from the target.
Feeling ashamed for not producing results despite advice, Louise gently rubbed my back.
“Don’t be so down. It’s okay. You can get results little by little from now on. Magic control is also a matter of talent, and it’s amazing you got any results in such a short time.”
Her comforting words were kind, but it seemed I lacked talent for magic.

I recalled what Louise said: many students were more talented than me, but most couldn’t graduate. No matter how talented in other areas, if you can’t draw out magic power, you’re worthless as a Valkyrie.
In the current reality where magic power is essential to fight Gijuu, no matter how talented you are in combat, without magic power, it’s meaningless.
“Maybe I don’t have the talent to handle magic.”
I complained, and Louise patted my back hard.
“No negative talk allowed! Ren, you need to be more positive. If your magic control improved even a little, you just need to grasp the knack now.”
“If I become more positive, will my magic power output improve?”
“If you got any results, you should try it. Besides, you just started; it’s no good to expect big results right away.”
I gave a wry smile at her words. I had been too impatient.
“You’re right. I’ll try a bit harder.”
Louise beamed.
“Yeah, that’s the best. I’ll look for some useful books too. Let’s work hard together, Ren.”
“Yes!”
A rumor was spreading around the academy, centered on Class 5.
Two female students were chatting in the hallway.
“Did you hear? The humanoid weapon experiment they’re running here has already failed six times.”
“They should just give up. Trying to militarize a man is impossible. We Valkyries should be left in charge.”
They mocked how desperate men were to regain their place on the battlefield. To them, the development team’s efforts probably looked like a waste.
At that moment, Louise was passing by, carrying the book she was taking to me.
(Ren’s bad rumors are spreading more than I thought.)
Trying not to listen, she tried to leave quickly, but the two girls blocked her path.
“Wait, Louise.”
“Where are you headed now?”
Though they knew her situation, they asked deliberately.
Louise hugged the book and answered.
“...I’m going to deliver this to Ren.”
The girls glanced at the book and looked suspicious. They hadn’t expected it was for the male pilot everyone was talking about.
Ignoring the book, they scolded Louise for her actions.
“Enough, Louise. I’m saying this because you’re in Class 5 with us, but he’s different from us.”
“Yeah, yeah. If you get involved, nothing good will come of it. There are rumors some girls say he tricked them. If this keeps up, you won’t get transferred in.”
“They say other classes are skeptical of male pilots too. And if you get close, rumors will say you’re involved with him. Whether true or not, you know such rumors would be fatal for us, right?”
Hearing their words, Louise looked down.
“I know that well. Valkyries aren’t supposed to be involved with men... But Ren and I are friends, and it’s a pure relationship, so there’s nothing to worry about.”
The girls exchanged glances and then pressed her.
“It’s about what others think. You failed the Boots Cat scout, and you’re still not learning?”
“You know turning other classes against you lowers your transfer chances, right? Then you should cut ties immediately.”
After saying their piece, they left Louise behind. She hugged the book tightly, trembling.
“...I understand better than anyone.”
In the corner of the hangar we were borrowing, I slumped on a training bench. I had pushed myself beyond the prepared menu, and by the end, my muscles were swollen and drenched in sweat.
The Thunderbolt wasn’t in the hangar. The development team had taken it to another lab for adjustments.
I stared at my trembling right hand. To get it to feel like my own, I had trained to my limit. But the limbs and organs created from Gijuu cells hadn’t fulfilled my hopes.
Even by the sixth experiment, the output hadn’t increased; it had continued to decline. Since the third experiment, when I got three times the output, it had been falling steadily.
I was told the upper management was considering scrapping the Prometheus Project because of this, and I was losing my sense of purpose.
Dr. Allison said they pulled the experimental machine out of the academy because they were thinking about canceling the project.
There was nothing left for me.
“What should I do... How can I produce magic power?”
Beside me lay a pile of books I had devoured. Besides the ones Louise recommended, I had bought and read others myself.
Yet none led to results. The more I failed, the farther the image of success drifted away.
Now, I couldn’t even believe in myself.
“Why can’t I fill the gap? How can I make up what I lack?”
I clenched my now-weak right hand tightly. No matter how much I tried to be positive, the deep part of my subconscious remained negative.
It found every possible failure and told me I wasn’t enough.
No matter how many books I read or how much I practiced what they said, nothing changed.
“Am I no good?”
I endured painful surgeries and rehabilitation to prove my worth. The frustration of failing to do so welled up inside me, an emotion I had never felt even on the harshest battlefields.
As I hung my head, my watch alarm sounded. The electronic beep echoed hollowly through the empty hangar, and I slowly stood.
“It’s time for the next training.”
I left the hangar with heavy steps and headed to the academy pool.
The pool late at night.
When I asked the academy for permission to use it for training, they allowed me only during hours when female students didn’t use it.
They set some conditions, and the lighting was limited. The indoor pool was dim and eerie. It felt like harassment from outsiders, but I was still grateful for the permission.
“I have to increase the time I spend training related to magic power, even if just a little.”
I finished warming up and was about to enter the pool when footsteps echoed inside.
The dim room was brighter from moonlight through the windows than from the weak lighting.
Turning around, I saw the source of the footsteps emerging from the darkness of the indoor pool.
It was Lieutenant Hayase, dressed in the academy’s designated swimsuit.
She didn’t look surprised to see me and stretched as she walked.
Hayase seemed to be smiling faintly.
“Oh? I didn’t expect someone else here.”
“That’s what I should say, Lieutenant Hayase. I have permission to use this time. Why are you here?”
I had permission because female students didn’t use the pool at this hour, but Hayase’s presence changed things.
She shifted her gaze from me to the upper left and answered.
“I suddenly felt like swimming.”
A sudden mood? Sure, there are days you feel like swimming, but I never expected it to overlap with the time I had permission.
Seeing my confusion, Hayase blushed for some reason.
“Or what? Are you saying I can’t swim here?”
I had permission from the academy, but I was still an outsider. Compared to her, an ace with privileges, my permission was meaningless.
“If you say that to someone with privileges like you, I can’t argue.”
“Privileges?”
Hayase tilted her head as I passed by and tried to leave the pool area. She probably didn’t want to swim with me, and if I couldn’t swim, staying here was a waste of time.
But Hayase grabbed my right arm.
“Wait. You have permission, right? Then there’s no need for you to leave.”
“Huh? But—”
“Just swim together. Or do you not want to be with me?”
[img]https://i.imgur.com/aCwEmWR.jpeg]

Lieutenant Hayase, standing in her swimsuit with her right hand on her hip, struck a pose that revealed a well-toned body. Since coming to this academy, I had been repeatedly surprised by the physiques of the female students. Their muscle mass wasn’t large—probably less than that of an average female soldier. Yet, their physical abilities surpassed those of even the toughest soldiers. Hairset and MC often saved pictures of gravure models and beautiful women on their devices, but many of these girls had appearances that rivaled those models. Lieutenant Hayase, bathed in moonlight, was more beautiful than any model Hairset had shown me. And yet, she was a guardian of humanity, fighting against the vicious Gijuu. Her slender, light frame that exhibited such astonishing physical prowess was personally fascinating to me. Since I had never had the chance to see her up close like this, I apparently found myself staring intently.
Hayase, standing confidently, twisted her body and covered her chest with both hands.
“Hey, hey, don’t stare at me so much. It’s really embarrassing, you know…”
“My apologies. I was simply taken aback by your proposal, Lieutenant Hayase.”
She turned her back to me but glanced over her shoulder.
“Well? I felt quite a rude gaze coming from you.”
Apparently, my stare had made her uncomfortable. I should apologize.
“I’m sorry. I was admiring your beautifully toned physique. Valkyries who can exert more strength than sturdy soldiers with such bodies truly are amazing.”
Hayase’s cheeks twitched as she blushed.
“Are you trying to compliment me?”
“To me, it was meant as a compliment.”
Hayase turned her face away from me and let out a big sigh.

While I was silently swimming laps alone in the night pool, Lieutenant Hayase floated on her back in a different lane. She didn’t seem to intend to swim and had just been floating there for some time. I finished swimming fifty meters and tried to steady my ragged breathing. Since it was just the two of us today, I could swim continuously, turning at the wall underwater. But I was tired, and the results weren’t what I wanted.
“This level is nowhere near enough. I have to… I have to be able to draw out more magic power.”
I told myself this and pushed my body for another lap. Just then, Hayase spoke.
“I’ve been wondering about something for a while now.”
I hadn’t noticed her approach and turned around in surprise. She smiled, seemingly amused by my reaction.
“Don’t be so startled. Isn’t it true that skilled soldiers never let their backs get taken?”
I didn’t think of myself as skilled, but I had to admit it was a fault not to notice her approach.
“Apologies. I must be showing signs of fatigue. But I’m not a skilled soldier.”
Hayase rested her body against the lane divider rope and looked at me comfortably.
“You’re too hard on yourself. Well, anyway… why have you been swimming nonstop?”

When asked why I was swimming, I hesitated for a moment, unsure what to say. I had consulted Louise, but was it okay to reveal classified information to Lieutenant Hayase as well? Perhaps my hesitation showed on my face, because Hayase seemed to understand.
“You can’t answer, huh? Well, I can guess. You’re struggling with your magic power output, aren’t you?”
I turned my face away from Hayase, who was well-informed about the development team’s affairs.
“You seem quite knowledgeable. Did you look into it?”
I spoke with a sharp edge, but Hayase snorted and then smiled without a trace of mockery.
“I’m not going to tell you. You have to figure it out yourself.”
For a moment, I thought that sounded insincere, but her gaze was utterly serious. I think I was momentarily captivated by those eyes.
Hayase asked about my current situation.
“Do you understand why you failed?”
I could have kept silent, citing confidentiality, but I had no way to break through my current predicament. So, I answered while withholding as much information as possible.
“It’s all because of my own inadequacy.”
“Inadequacy? Can’t you be more specific?”
She seemed surprised by my answer and wasn’t convinced.

“I did my best. I read the recommended books and kept training. But it was no use. No matter how hard I tried, I remained negative… I couldn’t get myself into the perfect condition before the experiment. I hate this inadequate self.”

I had tried every training I could think of, but the results didn’t follow. Even during experiments, my magic power output never reached the target, and failure kept piling up. As I looked down at the water’s surface, memories of all my hardships flooded back: surgeries, rehab, days at the academy… and countless training sessions. I didn’t want to believe it was all for nothing, but if this was the result, I had no choice but to accept it.
Hayase spoke with an exasperated tone.
“You thought reading self-help books and swimming would boost your magic power? Are you stupid?”
“...Lieutenant Hayase?”
When I looked up at her face, she was genuinely exasperated.
“Do you seriously think you can succeed without a positive mindset? The thing is, if negative people could become positive just by reading a book, it wouldn’t be such a struggle.”

Hayase dove under the lane rope to cross over, then surfaced in my lane. She pushed her hair back with both hands, shaking off the water, then shook her head. Droplets she scattered landed on my face. Hayase placed her left hand on my right shoulder. She moved unnervingly close—our noses were just centimeters apart.
“That essence of yours won’t change easily. You understand that, right?”
“Th-that is…”
I wanted to change. But I couldn’t. And I saw no hope of changing in the future. Hayase shook me as if urging me to answer.
“Ren Hifumi… why are you here?”
“For the mission. I volunteered for the Prometheus Project—”

Before I could finish, Hayase grabbed my left shoulder with her right hand and pinned me against the wall. My overworked body was at its limit, and I couldn’t shake her off. She seemed angry with me. Her anger grew, yet her eyes somehow looked sad.

“We’re here by our own will—to fight Gijuu. Everyone who graduated from middle school here is a warrior. We’re here to become Valkyries and fight. But you? You’re here just because you were ordered. I don’t like that.”
I could understand why Hayase disliked me, but I was here as a soldier. That fact wouldn’t change.
“I’m a soldier. I cannot disobey orders.”
Her grip on my shoulders tightened.

“It doesn’t matter! Warrior or soldier, it’s the same. Are you fighting just because you were ordered? That’s why your magic power won’t respond. That experimental machine must have suffered being piloted by a soldier without will like you.”
I tried to grab her wrist with my left hand and shake her off, but she resisted and I couldn’t break free.
“I have the will to fight. I do! But my magic power output didn’t improve at all. I tried everything and still failed!”

My gaze naturally fell on my regenerated right hand—the one grown from Gijuu cells. It was a hateful existence to me, but I underwent surgery because I heard it could help fight Gijuu. Yet, I was frustrated beyond measure that I couldn’t do anything and failed. If I had at least left valuable data for the experiment, I might have accepted it despite the regret. But I hadn’t achieved anything yet.
Hayase’s anger seemed to lessen somewhat.
“You’ve been making excuses about being a soldier and following orders, but you’re not answering the important part.”
“Important part?”
Her provocative expression vanished, replaced by one that seemed to appraise me.
“What did you hope to gain by volunteering for such a dangerous, low-success-rate human experiment?”
“That is… I had no choice but to bet on the success of the human experiment because otherwise I would have died. Also, I thought this project was meaningful for humanity.”
“To endure painful surgery and rehab? Some even died unable to bear it. Yet you endured. …Did you do it just because of orders or such shallow reasons?”

Being told that my ‘for humanity’ reason was shallow stung. Normally, I might have been furious, but I felt she had seen through the fact that I lacked a true motive of ‘for humanity’ and couldn’t argue back. Hayase’s blue eyes, shining even in the dim indoor pool, seemed to peer into my deepest psyche. As I felt myself drawn into those eyes, a familiar voice suddenly echoed.
“You really like goddesses, huh? No matter how much you stare, they won’t look your way.”

It was my squad leader’s teasing words from the battlefield, where I often looked up at the sky. Whenever I had free time, I searched for Valkyries on the battlefield. I didn’t even know why. It didn’t feel like admiration. Unintentionally, I was forced to confront that old self. What was I thinking as I looked up at the Valkyries? The feeling I harbored wasn’t something positive like admiration. Generally, it might be called ugly—a dark, swirling emotion that Hayase’s blue eyes seemed to relentlessly question. If I put that feeling into words, ironically it would be “envy,” close to my callsign. I envied those who soared high above the battlefield. I wanted that same power. I wanted to fight just like them.
“I joined the experiment because—”
Hesitating to speak, Hayase shook me impatiently.
“Say it quickly. Or will you be satisfied if I just say it was orders?”

I was growing frustrated with Hayase, who pressed me without knowing the circumstances. If she wanted to know so badly, I’d tell her. Grabbing both of her wrists, I unleashed the jealousy and everything else bottled inside me.

“Then I’ll say it. I’ve always envied you Valkyries! You who freely fly above us and fight Second Class and higher Gijuu! We were stuck on the ground, barely able to handle Third Class. And yet, Third Class is nothing to you!”
As I vented my frustrations, I felt Hayase relax her grip. But she never looked away from me.
“Yes, envy. I’ve envied you! I’ve always resented you who have powers we can never obtain… So when I heard I could fight like you, I volunteered.”

At that time, if I refused, I would have just been waiting to die. Knowing that volunteering meant harsh surgery and rehab, I accepted out of envy for the Valkyries. I was so excited after letting it all out that I was breathing heavily. At some point, I even switched to using “I” as my pronoun and regretted it. Regaining my composure, I averted my gaze from Hayase, who was silently watching me.
“Do you understand? My reasons for volunteering are trivial and personal—I volunteered out of envy for you.”
I thought it was a foolish story. I volunteered because I envied the Valkyries, endured harsh surgery and rehab, and survived. As I looked down, Hayase grabbed my hair and forcibly lifted my face.
“If that’s your reason, why are you looking down? Raise your head.”
“…Huh?”
“It’s fine. Even if you’re negative, if you can push through with that, there’s potential.”
At first, I didn’t understand what she meant. Hayase kept a serious expression.
“If you came this far just on envy, you might have a chance to match us. But if you keep pretending, it won’t work. You have to throw your true feelings into it, or your magic power won’t respond.”
She said this while looking at my right hand. Her left hand overlapped mine and gently squeezed it—the right hand created from Gijuu cells, despised by the girls of Class 5.
“Envy? That’s perfectly fine. What you need to do isn’t to fake positivity, but to accept yourself—even if you’re negative. Then your magic power will respond.”
Before I knew it, our bodies were pressed close together in the pool. I could feel a faint warmth from Hayase where we touched. Our lips were almost touching, and I was startled.
“Lieutenant Hayase… um, this close is a bit…”
When I calmly pointed it out, she seemed to notice and blushed, stepping back. Yet, her left hand, still holding my right, seemed reluctant to let go.
“A-anyway, that’s how it is!”

She said that and turned her back, heading out of the pool. I caught a glimpse of her profile, which seemed to be smiling. I hurried to follow, but my overtraining left me weak. So I called out loudly.
“Lieutenant Hayase, didn’t you hate yourself? Why are you giving me advice?”
Hayase, now out of the pool and still with her back to me, answered.
“What I dislike is the project you joined. Prometheus or whatever it’s called—I can’t accept a plan that allows human experimentation.”

She muttered complaints or grumbles, something like, “What do you think we’re here for?” Depending on how you heard it, it might sound like she only accepted Valkyries. But I didn’t think she meant it that way. From her character, I no longer thought she was a bad person.
I called out to her as she walked away.
“Thank you very much, Lieutenant Hayase!”
She stopped once, turned her upper body, and smiled.
“…I hope you succeed next time.”
With that, she left the indoor pool. While she remained opposed to the Prometheus Project itself, she apparently didn’t hold such bad feelings toward me personally. But that brought up one problem.
“…I hope this prediction turns out wrong.”
Louise, coming out of the school building, ran into Maya, whose hair was slightly wet.
“Lieutenant Hayase!?”
Seeing Louise’s surprised face, Maya showed a clearly displeased expression.
“What are you doing here at this hour?”
Her gaze was fixed on the book titles Louise was holding, and Maya didn’t even try to hide her disgust. When asked what she was doing in the library late at night, Louise answered.
“I heard Ren’s training was going on until late… And Lieutenant Hayase, what are you doing here? Don’t tell me you’re—”
Louise hugged the stack of books she had taken from the library.
“This isn’t any of your business. And seriously, you’re still recommending those books to him? It’s cruel to tell someone so negative to be positive.”
In response, Louise clearly stated her opinion.
“Ren is a positive person. He’s going through some things now, but I believe he’s basically optimistic.”
Louise had built a friendship with Ren in Class 5 and had a good grasp of his character. That’s why she was confident this was the most effective method.
“Right now, that’s not true. If you really want him to succeed, you should advise him to accept himself, even if negative.”
“That kind of temporary fix won’t work… Are you trying to use Ren up, Lieutenant Hayase?”
Maya overreacted to the phrase “use up.” Her hair slightly puffed up as if standing on end, and she furrowed her brows and glared.
“Use him up? You’re quite the one to say that.”

“Because that’s how it is, right? You only show temporary solutions and don’t see the real Ren. It’s too cruel to care only about results. If Ren were like us… you know that a half-baked success would be deadly.”

Louise’s accusatory gaze closed the distance between them rapidly. Maya closed the roughly three-meter gap in an instant and grabbed Louise’s shoulder. Louise’s clothes were twisted as Maya pulled her closer. Maya’s blue eyes were those of a battle-hardened Valkyrie.
“Spouting shallow lines so smoothly! That’s why I’ve hated you since middle school.”
This time, Louise refused to back down and resisted Maya.
“That’s what I say, Lieutenant Hayase. I wanted to get along, but you hated me and pushed me away.”

Louise pushed Maya away. Maya looked surprised but quickly wore a combative smile. As an experienced ace, Maya’s intimidation was harsh even for Louise. Suppressing the urge to flee, Louise retorted boldly.
“You’re the one who’s obsessed, aren’t you? Why do you interfere with us? Why do you keep bothering Ren? What do you want?”

Perhaps sensing Louise’s different attitude, Maya stopped intimidating and took a cautious stance. She opened her mouth to answer but ultimately said nothing. Louise showed a strength of will unlike usual.
“Lieutenant Hayase, I’m not giving in this time. I’ll protect Ren.”
Maya seemed deflated by Louise’s words.
“Fine… do as you like.”
Having gotten through the moment, Louise sighed deeply and headed for the hangar.
“I wonder if Ren’s okay… I hope Hayase didn’t say anything to him.”
